sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Cutoff 20 October 2026; standalone Indian GAAP/AS accounts. Last observed October 16 close ₹176, not a live quote. September capital reconciliation confirms 7.5 m shares, implying ₹132 cr dated equity value. Five-year nominal INR horizon and 15% analyst equity hurdle; ₹5 lakh illustrative liquidity reference cannot be matched exactly with ₹176,000 board lots. Historical statement confidence is high; capital-return and governance interpretation moderate; liquidity assessment is conditional and conservative, with live depth unobserved. [S1][CAP][M1]

Gate conclusions: G 1 Integrity: Material family compensation, export-channel commission and leased land are quantified; no reviewed evidence establishes diversion. Independent transaction benchmarking remains open. G 2 Financial reliability: Three-year cash history and capital-return proxies reconstructed. Grouping and gratuity-opening adjustments do not overturn cash conclusions. No critical financial-reliability failure established. G 3 Funding: Base/bear/severe annual financing models include capex, working capital and debt interest; severe stress requires new funding, not automatically available. G 4 Tradability: Listed since September 2022, no migration/suspension found in reviewed period, and all market dates present. Stage I ESM, large board lot and unobserved depth warrant L 2; conditional estimate is not an executable quote.

Evidence confidence: historical_financials: high; governance: medium; capital_returns: medium; forecast_and_cash_availability: medium for bounded estimates; outcomes uncertain; implementation: medium for conservative reference-position estimate; live spreads not observed; overall_weakest_material: medium for conditional scores; not an assurance of executable liquidity. sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: Precision valve/pump components, shafts/stems, hard-facing and assemblies. FY 26 export product sales ₹36.8258 cr, domestic ₹2.3585 cr, plus services/incentives/freight. Export-origin tracing and specifications are central to customer acceptance. Industry geography is not customer diversification: top-customer share remains unverified. Outsourced operations supplement a 68,000 sqft facility; count in-house machining versus outsourced value added before estimating capacity.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Mechanism: qualified precision parts and traceable material reduce switching convenience. Evidence: reported long relationships, ARDE supplies and specified CNC/VMC equipment. Durability depends on rejection rates, customer audits and repeat part numbers, not certifications alone. Failure: a qualified rival meets tolerances at lower total cost or customer insources. Market share and pricing premium ND, so useful but contestable capability earns MOAT 5. Gala Precision is an operating comparator for qualified industrial components, not a direct machining-multiple peer: its FY 26 annual report describes springs, high-tensile fasteners and washers, over 175 customers and 25 export countries. Its product mix and much larger ₹314.30 cr revenue differ from Ameya valve/pump components and ₹40.24 cr sales. Qualification, customer diversification, rejection rates and incremental capacity cash returns are more meaningful comparisons than adopting its traded multiple. [PEER1]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: FY 23/FY 24/FY 25/FY 26 revenue ₹28.5076/34.0343/38.5883/40.2379 cr. Additions ₹5.5267/4.5540/1.6496 cr; three-year CAGR 12.17%. Five/ten-year CAGR ND, not zero. Latest growth 4.27%; exports+8.35% but domestic product sales−34.56%. Price/volume/FX bridge is not disclosed sufficiently to assert organic volume growth. No acquisition contribution identified in reviewed statements, not a guarantee none exists. REV 6 uses historical three-year anchor without an opportunistic latest-year upgrade.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: The expansion case depends on qualified export parts and actual customer orders, not the 20% reserved floor space alone. The modeled base funds 5% annual capex and working capital at 45% of sales; growth must earn its funding cost. Reported EBIT/capital employed is ₹7.6653/33.1859 cr (23.10%) versus ₹6.0315/27.4204 cr (22.00%). Excluding all other income, including possibly operational FX, gives EBIT ₹6.4442/5.1153 cr. At assumed 25% tax, FY 26 operating NOPAT ₹4.83315 cr over average total capital ₹30.30315 cr is 15.95%. One-year incremental NOPAT/added total capital is (6.4442−5.1153)×75%/(33.1859−27.4204)=17.29%. These are conservative aggregate proxies, not mature-cohort ROIC, and can deteriorate if receivables or government refunds are impaired. No treasury deduction is used to manufacture an exceptionally high return. [S1]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: FY 26 directors Shirish/Bipin Pande remuneration ₹0.60/0.564 cr totals ₹1.164 cr,20.8%PAT. Related Ameya Europe commission ₹1.8626 cr,5.06%export product sales, versus ₹1.6285 cr FY 25; imports ₹0.2512 cr versus ₹1.4012 cr. Family rent ₹0.0816 cr total. Assess channel services and benchmark commission, not presume abuse. Cash capex and current equipment are observable outcomes; no original utilization/revenue targets were verified, so no fabricated promise-delivery table. Tax contingency ₹0.0313 cr is small relative to equity ₹33.0078 cr; it is not a critical integrity hold.

sections.text:
FY 24/FY 25/FY 26 PAT ₹2.9616/4.4296/5.5874 cr; CFO ₹6.1812/5.9830/1.9548 cr; capex ₹0.2972/6.2487/2.0124 cr; FCF ₹5.8840/−0.2657/−0.0576 cr. sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: At dated ₹176 and verified 7.5 m shares, market value is ₹132 cr and reported FY 26 P/E 23.63 x. Linked base/bear/bull terminal prices ₹190.05/₹38.68/₹383.20, with annualized returns 1.55%/-26.14%/16.84%. Base 15%-hurdle entry arithmetic is ₹94.49, conditional on 10% growth, 16% operating EBIT, funded capex and collections. It is not an execution recommendation or precise intrinsic value. Full cash, debt and sensitivity rows are retained. [S1][CAP][M1]

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: Bear terminal price ₹38.68; severe terminal ₹0.00 with modeled funding need. Collection deterioration and stranded capacity can create material impairment despite low opening debt. The severe model assumes 25% then 10% sales contraction, 2% EBIT margin, working capital at 75% of sales and ₹2.5 cr extra cash unavailability. New debt is modeled at 12%; unavailable bank funding could require equity dilution or worse recovery. [S1]

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: From ₹176,5×/10×in five years requires 37.97%/58.49%price CAGR. At unchanged shares and 20×terminal P/E, required EPS ₹44/₹88, or 42.65%/63.86%annual EPS growth from ₹7.45. With unchanged FY 26 PATmargin 13.89%, the implied revenue is about ₹237.7/475.3 cr versus ₹40.24 cr today. This is a reverse mathematical requirement, not a forecast; no verified capacity/customer/funding evidence supports it.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: 1.Revenue additions versus ₹1.65 cr FY 26;2.export/domestic and price-volume mix;3.receivables end-days versus 114.3 and aged ₹0.0806 cr;4.subsequent cash receipts;5.government balances ₹5.10 cr;6.FDencumbrance and cash-credit headroom;7.Ameya Europe commission/exports 5.06%;8.qualified part wins/rejection and utilization;9.capex commissioning versus incrementalgrossprofit;10.director/RPTterms and share changes. Analyst warning: receivable end-days>135 for two reporting periods without receipts evidence, or agedbalances>5%sales, would require renewed funding/impairment work; these are monitoring thresholds, not company guidance.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Completed review: modest-quality export manufacturer, not a verified compounder. Dated price does not meet the analyst hurdle in the linked base case. Conditional IAS is in the low-attractiveness band, with L 2 reflecting severe implementation friction. Lower valuation cannot cure a collection or connected-party economics failure. The ₹5 lakh reference is not a recommendation of position size.

Final published measures: BQS 5.5; GQS 5.8; IAS 3.125. Any change in price, funded cash deployment, share count or execution restrictions requires recomputation; these are conditional research classifications, not a trade instruction.

opening_bridge.working_capital_formula: Inventory + receivables + advances + prepaid expenses + government balances − payables − other liabilities − expense/salary/audit accruals; excludes income-tax payable and actuarial gratuity

assumption_basis: Base growth 10% is below FY23–26 12.19% CAGR, above latest 4.27%: it requires recovery, not extrapolation of the latest quarter.
Base EBIT margin 16% excludes all other income, approximately FY26 conservative operating margin. Bull margin 19% requires better utilization; bear 8% models operating deleverage.
45% base working capital is near the reconstructed opening requirement; bear/severe 60%/75% stress delayed export and government collections.
Capex 5% and depreciation 3% of sales approximate FY26 cash purchases and depreciation, and explicitly fund growth; ongoing dividend zero follows FY26 retention policy.
Cash reserve ₹2.5cr and exclusion of all investments avoid treating every financial asset as surplus. Bear/severe impose an additional ₹2.5cr cash haircut for FD restriction/recovery risk.
Debt funding shortfalls carry 12% pre-tax interest with 25% tax assumption; no automatic equity issuance. Inability to obtain modeled debt would mean further dilution or a worse outcome.
Terminal NOPAT multiples 12/16/20 are analyst sensitivities, not peer-derived fair values. All surplus future cash is counted once. Dated price is not executable.
